term: finite tests of complete Reaper tail clauses
definition: For every finite set I of natural-number indices, there is a total action predicate acts on Nat such that, for each n in I, acts n holds exactly when every m greater than n does not act. Each tested right-hand side ranges over the entire infinite tail, including untested indices. The action predicate can differ for different I. The recorded control conjoins this finite compatibility with the existing impossibility of one action predicate satisfying all indices.
note: Source-free mathematical test of the existing firing rule. Unlike Fin size schedules, only clause selection is finite, not the action domain or each clause's tail. This is not a counterexample to ordinary finitary propositional compactness: the tail clauses themselves have infinitary action dependence. No causal capacity, possible-world assembly, actual existence or adequate-explanation interpretation is established.
